storyHero.label: My Story
headline: Community services worker
Non-profit leader
Advocate
storyHero.intro: Jean Claude Muhire is a college-trained community services worker, dedicated non-profit leader, and chronic illness advocate. His work is grounded in two connected areas: Lived Experience, including chronic illness, resilience, belonging, and the realities of navigating systems not always built with care in mind, and Community Action, including advocacy, servant leadership, and the power of turning personal stories into support, awareness, and collective responsibility.

portrait.alt: Jean Claude Muhire smiling, in a black leather jacket

items.title: Born and raised
items.text: Jean Claude was born and raised in rural southern Rwanda, where he completed his primary and secondary education. He lost his biological mother at the age of 12 and was raised by his single grandmother during the difficult years following the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. Those early experiences brought hardship, but they also helped shape who he is today, strengthening his resilience, compassion, and commitment to serving others.
items.photoAlt: Jean Claude Muhire as a young boy, crouching and smiling, in a school uniform

items.title: Humanitarian and social work
items.text: Jean Claude’s commitment to community service began in 2012, when he served full-time as a volunteer responsible for communication and correspondence at the former Kimisagara Orphanage, which supported more than 250 orphans and vulnerable children in Rwanda. Although he was admitted to the University of Rwanda to study chemistry, his passion for serving others continued to pull him toward community work. During that time, he was also trained as a peer educator and facilitator with Kimisagara Youth Center, contributing to youth-focused efforts to raise awareness and prevent HIV/AIDS and drug abuse in partnership with Rwanda’s Ministry of Youth.

items.title: Love the Kids Rwanda
items.text: In 2015, Jean Claude founded Love the Kids Rwanda, a registered non-profit organization that provides scholarships for children from vulnerable families to attend school in Rwanda. Over the years, the organization has supported more than 250 young people, including students who have gone on to complete high school and university.
items.photoAlt: Children in yellow shirts playing a circle game, at a Love the Kids Rwanda gathering

items.title: Leader of the Year
items.text: Winner of the Africa Youth Awards 2016, Leader of the Year. A year earlier, he was the International Winner of the 2015 Global Dialogues contest.
items.photoAlt: Jean Claude Muhire, in a photo published with the 2016 Africa Youth Awards news

items.title: Mandela Washington Fellow
items.text: His selection as a Mandela Washington Fellow through the U.S. Department of State’s Young African Leaders Initiative at Appalachian State University in North Carolina in 2018.
items.photoAlt: Jean Claude Muhire standing beside the Appalachian State University sign

items.title: Human Rights Prize
items.text: A laureate of the French Government’s Human Rights Prize in Paris in 2019.
items.photoAlt: Jean Claude Muhire speaking at a lectern at the French Ministry of Justice, where the 2019 Human Rights Prize was presented

items.title: Final-stage kidney disease
items.text: In 2020, Jean Claude learned that he had reached the final stage of chronic kidney disease. Doctors told him that a kidney transplant was his only path forward, but the surgery could not be performed in his home country. With limited access to specialized care, his condition posed a serious risk to his life.
items.photoAlt: Jean Claude Muhire resting during a dialysis session in hospital

items.title: A kidney from Marie Reine
items.text: Marie Reine, his girlfriend at the time and now his wife, agreed to donate one of her kidneys. With the support of a close friend, Jean Claude launched a GoFundMe campaign that raised more than $20,000 in less than five days. He and Marie Reine then traveled to Egypt, where, on November 30, he received a successful transplant.
items.photoAlt: An aeroplane wing seen through a window at sunrise (provisional stock photo)

items.title: A wedding
items.text: On August 12, 2021, Jean Claude and Marie Reine held their civil wedding.
items.photoAlt: Jean Claude Muhire lifting his bride’s veil during their wedding ceremony

items.title: A new home
items.text: In 2022, Jean Claude immigrated to Canada, where he now lives with his wife and daughter.
items.photoAlt: Autumn maple leaves over a quiet street corner (provisional stock photo)

today.heading: Today
today.text: Today, he speaks to audiences about what it means to lead from lived experience, build meaningful community, and transform hardship into purpose. He brings a deep human perspective to conversations on leadership, health equity, community support, resilience, and purpose, reminding audiences that no one should have to face their hardest moments alone and that support from others can help people survive, heal, and move forward.
